question:
(a) Obtain the expression for motional emf induced in a conducting rod of length $l$ moving with velocity $v$ perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$.
(b) How will the induced emf change if the velocity of the rod is doubled? Justify your answer.

options.A:
$\varepsilon=\dfrac{Bv}{l}$
If velocity is doubled, the emf becomes half.
options.B:
$\varepsilon=Blv$
Since $\varepsilon\propto v$, doubling the velocity doubles the induced emf to $2\varepsilon$.
options.C:
$\varepsilon=\dfrac{Bl}{v}$
If velocity is doubled, the emf remains unchanged.
options.D:
$\varepsilon=Bv^2l$
If velocity is doubled, the emf becomes four times.
